paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה הָיָה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית לֵאמֹ֑ר לֵ֚ךְ הֵרָאֵ֣ה אֶל־אַחְאָ֔ב וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה מָטָ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass after many days that the word of YHWH came to Eliyahu in the third year, saying, "Go, show yourself to Ach'av, and I will give rain upon the face of the ground."

notes.official: *baššānâ haššəlîšîṯ* 'in the third year' (of the drought, counted from 17:1). Luke 4:25 and James 5:17 give 'three years and six months', a traditional figure (cf. Dan 7:25; 12:7). Shomron (v 2) = Samaria, Ach'av's capital.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵֽלִיָּ֔הוּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת אֶל־אַחְאָ֑ב וְהָרָעָ֖ב חָזָ֥ק בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: So Eliyahu went to show himself to Ach'av. And the famine was severe in Shomron.

notes.official: Names in this chapter: Eliyahu = Elijah, Ach'av = Ahab, Ovadyahu = Obadiah, Izevel = Jezebel, Karmel = Carmel, Qishon = Kishon, Yizre'el = Jezreel, Shomron = Samaria (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *wəhārāʿāḇ ḥāzāq* 'and the famine was severe'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אַחְאָ֔ב אֶל־עֹבַדְיָ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וְעֹבַדְיָ֗הוּ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֛א אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And Ach'av called Ovadyahu, who was over the household. (Now Ovadyahu feared YHWH greatly;

notes.official: Ovadyahu = Obadiah, 'servant of Yah'. The narrator's note that he 'feared YHWH greatly' puts a Yahwist at the head of Ach'av's household (*ʾăšer ʿal-habbāyiṯ*, the palace steward, cf. Isa 22:15). The parenthesis runs to the end of v 4.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ בְּהַכְרִ֣ית אִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֖ת נְבִיאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֨ח עֹבַדְיָ֜הוּ מֵאָ֣ה נְבִאִ֗ים וַֽיַּחְבִּיאֵ֞ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְכִלְכְּלָ֖ם לֶ֥חֶם וָמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: for when Izevel cut off the prophets of YHWH, Ovadyahu took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men to a cave, and provided them with bread and water.)

notes.official: *ḥămiššîm ʾîš bammĕʿārâ*: the MT has a single 'fifty men in the cave', while v 13 has the distributive *ḥămiššîm ḥămiššîm* 'by fifties'. The LXX and Peshitta read the distributive here too. The translation follows the MT words and renders them in the sense v 13 requires, 'fifty men to a cave' (ASV 'by fifty in a cave'); see `mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`. *bəhaḵrîṯ ʾîzeḇel* 'when Izevel cut off': Izevel = Jezebel.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֶל־עֹ֣בַדְיָ֔הוּ לֵ֤ךְ בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶל־כָּל־מַעְיְנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־הַנְּחָלִ֑ים אוּלַ֣י ׀ נִמְצָ֣א חָצִ֗יר וּנְחַיֶּה֙ ס֣וּס וָפֶ֔רֶד וְל֥וֹא נַכְרִ֖ית מֵהַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Ach'av said to Ovadyahu, "Go through the land, to all the springs of water and to all the brooks; perhaps we may find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, so that we do not lose any of the animals."

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְחַלְּק֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לַֽעֲבָר־בָּ֑הּ אַחְאָ֞ב הָלַ֨ךְ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אֶחָד֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְעֹֽבַדְיָ֛הוּ הָלַ֥ךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ־אֶחָ֖ד לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: So they divided the land between them to pass through it; Ach'av went one way by himself, and Ovadyahu went another way by himself.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י עֹבַדְיָ֙הוּ֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַיַּכִּרֵ֙הוּ֙ וַיִּפֹּ֣ל עַל־פָּנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה אֲדֹנִ֥י אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And as Ovadyahu was on the way, behold, Eliyahu met him; and he recognized him and fell on his face and said, "Is it you, my lord Eliyahu?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אָ֑נִי לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "It is I. Go, say to your lord, 'Behold, Eliyahu is here.'"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה חָטָ֑אתִי כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה נֹתֵ֧ן אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֛ בְּיַד־אַחְאָ֖ב לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And he said, "What sin have I committed, that you would give your servant into the hand of Ach'av, to kill me?

paragraphs.text: חַ֣י ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אִם־יֶשׁ־גּ֤וֹי וּמַמְלָכָה֙ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־שָׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִ֥י שָׁם֙ לְבַקֶּשְׁךָ֔ וְאָמְר֖וּ אָ֑יִן וְהִשְׁבִּ֤יעַ אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ וְאֶת־הַגּ֔וֹי כִּ֖י לֹ֥א יִמְצָאֶֽכָּה׃

i18n.en: As YHWH your Elohim lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you; and when they said, 'He is not here,' he made the kingdom and the nation swear that they had not found you.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֑ר לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And now you are saying, 'Go, say to your lord, "Behold, Eliyahu is here."'

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֞ה אֲנִ֣י ׀ אֵלֵ֣ךְ מֵאִתָּ֗ךְ וְר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֤ה ׀ יִֽשָּׂאֲךָ֙ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־אֵדָ֔ע וּבָ֨אתִי לְהַגִּ֧יד לְאַחְאָ֛ב וְלֹ֥א יִֽמְצָאֲךָ֖ וַהֲרָגָ֑נִי וְעַבְדְּךָ֛ יָרֵ֥א אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה מִנְּעֻרָֽי׃

i18n.en: And it will come to pass, as soon as I have gone from you, that the ruach of YHWH will carry you I know not where; and when I come to tell Ach'av and he cannot find you, he will kill me — yet I your servant have feared YHWH from my youth.

notes.official: *wərûaḥ YHWH yiśśāʾăḵā ʿal ʾăšer lōʾ-ʾēḏāʿ* 'the ruach of YHWH will carry you I know not where'. *rûaḥ* means 'wind', 'breath' or 'spirit', and commentators divide here between a divine spirit and a 'wind of YHWH' (cf. Isa 40:7; Hos 13:15; Gray, *I & II Kings*, OTL). The ASV capital 'Spirit' brings in the later doctrine of a personal Holy Spirit. Following ezekiel-woh at Ezek 37:1 ('he brought me out by the ruach of YHWH'), the word is transliterated so that the ambiguity remains (`ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`, inferred). Ovadyahu's fear assumes that Eliyahu is known to vanish and reappear unpredictably; 2 Kgs 2:16 says the same thing about Eliyahu in almost the same words.

paragraphs.text: הֲלֹֽא־הֻגַּ֤ד לַֽאדֹנִי֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֔יתִי בַּהֲרֹ֣ג אִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֖ת נְבִיאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וָאַחְבִּא֩ מִנְּבִיאֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה מֵ֣אָה אִ֗ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֨ים חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וָאֲכַלְכְּלֵ֖ם לֶ֥חֶם וָמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Was it not told my lord what I did when Izevel killed the prophets of YHWH — how I hid a hundred men of the prophets of YHWH, by fifties in a cave, and provided them with bread and water?

notes.official: *ḥămiššîm ḥămiššîm* 'by fifties': the distributive that v 4 implies (see there). Ovadyahu's self-defence repeats the narrator's parenthesis of vv 3-4.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַֽאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֣ה אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַהֲרָגָֽנִי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And now you are saying, 'Go, say to your lord, "Behold, Eliyahu is here"'; and he will kill me."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵֽלִיָּ֔הוּ חַ֚י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָמַ֖דְתִּי לְפָנָ֑יו כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֵרָאֶ֥ה אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said, "As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him today."

notes.official: *ḥay YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ* 'As YHWH of hosts lives': the divine title rendered as in isaiah-woh (`yhwh-tsevaot-yhwh-of-hosts-kings`). Its grammar (a proper name in apparent construct) and the referent of the 'hosts' (armies, heavenly host) are disputed (Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982); 'hosts' leaves both senses open.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ עֹבַדְיָ֛הוּ לִקְרַ֥את אַחְאָ֖ב וַיַּגֶּד־ל֑וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחְאָ֖ב לִקְרַ֥את אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: So Ovadyahu went to meet Ach'av and told him; and Ach'av went to meet Eliyahu.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֛י כִּרְא֥וֹת אַחְאָ֖ב אֶת־אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֵלָ֔יו הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה עֹכֵ֥ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Ach'av saw Eliyahu, that Ach'av said to him, "Is it you, you troubler of Yisra'el?"

notes.official: *ʿōḵēr yiśrāʾēl* 'troubler of Yisra'el': *ʿkr* 'bring disaster on' is the verb of the Akhan story (Josh 7:25, the valley of Akhor). Eliyahu turns the charge back on Ach'av in v 18.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א עָכַ֙רְתִּי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י אִם־אַתָּ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ בַּֽעֲזָבְכֶם֙ אֶת־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַבְּעָלִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he said, "I have not troubled Yisra'el; but you have, and your father's house, in that you have forsaken the commandments of YHWH and you have gone after the Ba'als.

notes.official: *habbəʿālîm* 'the Ba'als' (ASV 'the Baalim'): the plural denotes local manifestations or images of Ba'al (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֨ח קְבֹ֥ץ אֵלַ֛י אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְאֶת־נְבִיאֵ֨י הַבַּ֜עַל אַרְבַּ֧ע מֵא֣וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֗ים וּנְבִיאֵ֤י הָֽאֲשֵׁרָה֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת אֹכְלֵ֖י שֻׁלְחַ֥ן אִיזָֽבֶל׃

i18n.en: Now therefore send and gather to me all Yisra'el at Mount Karmel, and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Ba'al, and the four hundred prophets of the Asherah, who eat at Izevel's table."

notes.official: *nəḇîʾê habbaʿal* / *nəḇîʾê hāʾăšērâ*: Hebrew writes both divine names with the article. English convention omits it for Ba'al (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-kings`). For Asherah the ASV keeps it, and so does this translation, because *ʾăšērâ* names both the goddess and her wooden cult object. Prophets who 'eat at Izevel's table' point to the goddess (`nevie-ha-asherah-prophets-of-the-asherah-1-kings-18-19`; Ugaritic background in the central `athirat-asherah-mother-goddess-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`). The 400 prophets of the Asherah do not appear again in the contest or in the slaughter of v 40, and some scholars regard the phrase as an addition (Cogan, *1 Kings*). Karmel = Carmel.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אַחְאָ֖ב בְּכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל־הַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶֽל׃

i18n.en: So Ach'av sent to all the children of Yisra'el and gathered the prophets together at Mount Karmel.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ עַד־מָתַ֞י אַתֶּ֣ם פֹּסְחִים֮ עַל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַסְּעִפִּים֒ אִם־יְהוָ֤ה הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְאִם־הַבַּ֖עַל לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־עָנ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu came near to all the people and said, "How long will you go limping between the two sides? If YHWH is the Elohim, follow him; but if Ba'al, follow him." And the people did not answer him a word.

notes.official:
*ʿaḏ-māṯay ʾattem pōsəḥîm ʿal-štê hassəʿippîm*: literally 'how long will you be limping (or hopping) on the two branches/crutches?'. *səʿippîm* is related to *sēʿăp̄îm* 'divided, double-minded' (Ps 119:113), and the image is of someone unable to settle. ASV 'go limping between the two sides' is kept; KJV 'halt between two opinions' is a paraphrase. The verb *psḥ* 'limp' returns at v 26 for the Ba'al prophets' dance.

*ʾim-YHWH hāʾĕlōhîm* 'If YHWH is the Elohim': the articular *hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the (true) Elohim' sets up the contest (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אֲנִ֞י נוֹתַ֧רְתִּי נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה לְבַדִּ֑י וּנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֔עַל אַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: Then Eliyahu said to the people, "I, I alone, am left a prophet of YHWH; but the prophets of Ba'al are four hundred and fifty men.

notes.official: *ʾănî nôṯartî nāḇîʾ ləYHWH ləḇaddî* 'I, I alone, am left a prophet of YHWH' is rhetorical, since Ovadyahu has hidden a hundred (v 13). Eliyahu repeats the claim at Horeb (19:10, 14), and YHWH corrects it there (19:18).

paragraphs.text: וְיִתְּנוּ־לָ֜נוּ שְׁנַ֣יִם פָּרִ֗ים וְיִבְחֲר֣וּ לָהֶם֩ הַפָּ֨ר הָאֶחָ֜ד וִֽינַתְּחֻ֗הוּ וְיָשִׂ֙ימוּ֙ עַל־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ימוּ וַאֲנִ֞י אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה ׀ אֶת־הַפָּ֣ר הָאֶחָ֗ד וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ עַל־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א אָשִֽׂים׃

i18n.en: Let them give us two bulls; and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood, but put no fire to it; and I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood, and put no fire to it.

paragraphs.text: וּקְרָאתֶ֞ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶקְרָ֣א בְשֵׁם־יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲנֶ֥ה בָאֵ֖שׁ ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֧עַן כָּל־הָעָ֛ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָֽר׃

i18n.en: And you call on the name of your elohim, and I will call on the name of YHWH; and the Elohim who answers by fire, he is the Elohim." And all the people answered and said, "The word is good."

notes.official:
*ûqərāʾṯem bəšēm ʾĕlōhêḵem* 'and you call on the name of your elohim': lower-case where the referent is Ba'al, capital where it is YHWH. Hebrew script has no case, and the distinction is an editorial device that keeps the Hebrew lexeme while marking the narrative's contrast (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`; precedent EXO-WOH-20:3 'other elohim'). ASV: 'your god'.

*wəhāyâ hāʾĕlōhîm ʾăšer-yaʿăneh ḇāʾēš hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the Elohim who answers by fire, he is the Elohim': the terms of the contest, answered by the confession of v 39.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ לִנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל בַּחֲר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם הַפָּ֤ר הָֽאֶחָד֙ וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רִאשֹׁנָ֔ה כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם הָרַבִּ֑ים וְקִרְאוּ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א תָשִֽׂימוּ׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to the prophets of Ba'al, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are the many; and call on the name of your elohim, but put no fire to it."

notes.official: *kî ʾattem hārabbîm* 'for you are the many'. *ʾĕlōhêḵem* 'your elohim' as in v 24 (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַ֠יִּקְחוּ אֶת־הַפָּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֣ן לָהֶם֮ וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֒ וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ בְשֵׁם־הַ֠בַּעַל מֵהַבֹּ֨קֶר וְעַד־הַצָּהֳרַ֤יִם לֵאמֹר֙ הַבַּ֣עַל עֲנֵ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה וַֽיְפַסְּח֔וּ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

i18n.en: And they took the bull which was given them, and they prepared it, and called on the name of Ba'al from morning until noon, saying, "O Ba'al, answer us!" But there was no voice, and no one answering. And they limped about the altar which had been made.

notes.official:
*ʾăšer-nāṯan lāhem* ... *ʾăšer ʿāśâ*: both verbs are singular and active ('which he gave them' ... 'which he had made'). They can be impersonal (ASV 'which was given them' ... 'which was made'), can refer to Eliyahu, or can be emended to plurals with some versions. The translation keeps the impersonal construal of the MT (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

*wayəpassəḥû* 'and they limped about': piel of *psḥ*, the verb of v 21 (cf. *pissēaḥ* 'lame', 2 Sam 9:13), probably describing a limping ritual dance (Gray, *I & II Kings*; Cogan). ASV 'leaped about' loses the echo, which the translation keeps. *ʾên qôl wəʾên ʿōneh* 'no voice, and no one answering' becomes a refrain (v 29).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֨י בַֽצָּהֳרַ֜יִם וַיְהַתֵּ֧ל בָּהֶ֣ם אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ קִרְא֤וּ בְקוֹל־גָּדוֹל֙ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא כִּ֣י שִׂ֧יחַ וְכִֽי־שִׂ֛יג ל֖וֹ וְכִֽי־דֶ֣רֶךְ ל֑וֹ אוּלַ֛י יָשֵׁ֥ן ה֖וּא וְיִקָֽץ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass at noon that Eliyahu mocked them and said, "Call with a loud voice, for he is an elohim! Either he is musing, or he has gone aside, or he is on a journey; perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened."

notes.official:
*kî-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ* 'for he is an elohim!': ironic, with lower-case 'elohim' for Ba'al (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`).

*kî śîaḥ wəḵî-śîḡ lô*: *śîaḥ* is 'musing, complaint, talk', and *śîḡ* occurs only here. ASV 'he has gone aside' takes it from *sûg* 'turn away'. A reading found in medieval Jewish commentary and argued by Rendsburg ('The Mock of Baal in 1 Kings 18:27', *CBQ* 50, 1988) takes 'gone aside' as a euphemism for relieving oneself. The translation keeps ASV 'he is musing, or he has gone aside', which leaves that reading available. The taunts (asleep, travelling) parody motifs of Ba'al mythology known from Ugarit, where Ba'al dies and is absent (Smith 2002).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וַיִּתְגֹּֽדְדוּ֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בַּחֲרָב֖וֹת וּבָֽרְמָחִ֑ים עַד־שְׁפָךְ־דָּ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they called with a loud voice and cut themselves, according to their custom, with swords and spears, until blood poured out upon them.

notes.official: *wayyiṯgōḏəḏû kəmišpāṭām* 'and they cut themselves, according to their custom': self-laceration in mourning or supplication is attested in Ugaritic texts (El and Anat mourning Ba'al, KTU 1.5 vi-1.6 i) and forbidden in Israel (Deut 14:1; Lev 19:28).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַֽצָּהֳרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֔וּ עַ֖ד לַעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וְאֵֽין־ק֥וֹל וְאֵין־עֹנֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין קָֽשֶׁב׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when noon was past, that they prophesied until the time of the offering up of the offering; but there was no voice, and no one answering, and no one paying heed.

notes.official:
*wayyiṯnabbəʾû* 'they prophesied': the hithpael of *nbʾ* describes ecstatic, frenzied behaviour (cf. Saul, 1 Sam 18:10, 'raved'). NRSV renders 'raved on'. The ASV 'prophesied' is kept so that the lexical link with *nāḇîʾ* 'prophet' stays visible (`navi-first-occurrence-abraham`).

*ʿaḏ laʿălôṯ hamminḥâ* 'until the time of the offering up of the offering': *minḥâ* (`minchah-shaah`) here is the regular afternoon offering of the temple day (cf. 2 Kgs 16:15 *minḥaṯ hāʿereḇ*). ASV supplies '[evening] oblation'. *wəʾên qəšeḇ* 'and no one paying heed' completes the refrain of v 26.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֤הוּ לְכָל־הָעָם֙ גְּשׁ֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וַיִּגְּשׁ֥וּ כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֵלָ֑יו וַיְרַפֵּ֛א אֶת־מִזְבַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה הֶהָרֽוּס׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to all the people, "Come near to me." And all the people came near to him. And he repaired the altar of YHWH that had been thrown down.

notes.official: *wayrappēʾ ʾeṯ-mizbaḥ YHWH hehārûs* 'he repaired the altar of YHWH that had been thrown down': Karmel had an old Yahwistic altar, torn down in the persecution (cf. 19:10, 14). Some scholars see vv 31-32a as a later expansion, because v 32 has Eliyahu build an altar anew.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ אֲבָנִ֔ים כְּמִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Ya'aqov, to whom the word of YHWH had come, saying, "Yisra'el shall be your name."

notes.official: The twelve stones and the quotation 'Yisra'el shall be your name' echo Gen 35:10 (cf. Gen 32:29) and Ex 24:4 (twelve pillars at Sinai). The altar stands for all twelve tribes, although the scene takes place in the northern kingdom. Ya'aqov = Jacob.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבְנֶ֧ה אֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֛ים מִזְבֵּ֖חַ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֣עַשׂ תְּעָלָ֗ה כְּבֵית֙ סָאתַ֣יִם זֶ֔רַע סָבִ֖יב לַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And with the stones he built an altar in the name of YHWH; and he made a trench around the altar, as large as would hold two se'ahs of seed.

notes.official: *kəḇêṯ sāʾtayim zeraʿ* 'as large as would hold two se'ahs of seed': probably the area sown with two se'ahs of seed, i.e. a measure of surface rather than of volume (Cogan, *1 Kings*; cf. Lev 27:16).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־הָֽעֵצִ֑ים וַיְנַתַּח֙ אֶת־הַפָּ֔ר וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־הָעֵצִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he arranged the wood, and cut the bull in pieces, and laid it on the wood.

notes.official: Versification: the MT ends 18:33 with the bull laid on the wood. ASV 18:33 already includes 'Fill four jars with water...', so ASV 18:34 contains only the second and third pourings. The translation follows the MT division (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִלְא֨וּ אַרְבָּעָ֤ה כַדִּים֙ מַ֔יִם וְיִֽצְק֥וּ עַל־הָעֹלָ֖ה וְעַל־הָעֵצִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁנוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁנ֔וּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שַׁלֵּ֖שׁוּ וַיְשַׁלֵּֽשׁוּ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt-offering and on the wood." And he said, "Do it a second time," and they did it a second time. And he said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.

notes.official: MT 18:34 = ASV 18:33b-34 (see v 33). *ʿal-hāʿōlâ* 'on the burnt-offering' (`olah-burnt-offering`). Pouring water three times, twelve jars in all, during a drought maximizes the difficulty of ignition. Some see in it rain-making ritual (Patai, 'The Control of Rain in Ancient Palestine', *HUCA* 14, 1939), though the narrative does not say so.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם סָבִ֖יב לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַתְּעָלָ֖ה מִלֵּא־מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the water ran around the altar; and he also filled the trench with water.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֗ה וַיִּגַּ֞שׁ אֵלִיָּ֣הוּ הַנָּבִיא֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָם֙ יִצְחָ֣ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיּ֣וֹם יִוָּדַ֗ע כִּֽי־אַתָּ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַאֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ ובדבריך [וּבִדְבָרְךָ֣] עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, at the time of the offering up of the offering, that Eliyahu the prophet came near and said, "O YHWH, the Elohim of Avraham, Yitzchaq, and Yisra'el, let it be known today that you are Elohim in Yisra'el, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things at your word.

notes.official:
*YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾaḇrāhām yiṣḥāq wəyiśrāʾēl*: the patriarchal title (`elohei-avraham-yitzchaq-veyaakov-patriarchal-god-formula-cross-corpus`), here with a single *ʾĕlōhê* and with 'Yisra'el' rather than 'Ya'aqov' (as in 1 Chr 29:18; 2 Chr 30:6), which ties the title to the twelve-stone altar of v 31.

*kî-ʾattâ ʾĕlōhîm bəyiśrāʾēl* 'that you are Elohim in Yisra'el': an anarthrous predicate, rendered without the article (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`).

Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ûḇiḏəḇāreyḵā* 'and by your words' / Qere *ûḇiḏḇārəḵā* 'and at your word'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *laʿălôṯ hamminḥâ* as in v 29.

paragraphs.text: עֲנֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ עֲנֵ֔נִי וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְאַתָּ֛ה הֲסִבֹּ֥תָ אֶת־לִבָּ֖ם אֲחֹרַנִּֽית׃

i18n.en: Answer me, O YHWH, answer me, that this people may know that you, YHWH, are the Elohim, and that you have turned their heart back again."

notes.official: *wəʾattâ hăsibbōṯā ʾeṯ-libbām ʾăḥōrannîṯ* 'and that you have turned their heart back again'. Most versions (ASV, NJPS) and commentators read this as YHWH turning the people back to himself. *ʾăḥōrannîṯ* 'backward' allows a minority reading, 'you turned their heart backward', i.e. YHWH himself caused the apostasy (discussed in rabbinic exegesis and by some moderns; cf. Isa 63:17). The majority construal is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּפֹּ֣ל אֵשׁ־יְהוָ֗ה וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶת־הָֽעֹלָה֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֖ים וְאֶת־הֶעָפָ֑ר וְאֶת־הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר־בַּתְּעָלָ֖ה לִחֵֽכָה׃

i18n.en: Then the fire of YHWH fell and consumed the burnt-offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.

notes.official:
*wattippōl ʾēš-YHWH* 'Then the fire of YHWH fell': a construct with the divine name, definite in Hebrew, governed by the new central `esh-yhwh-fire-of-yhwh`. The MT here does not read *ʾēš ʾĕlōhîm* 'fire of Elohim'. The central `esh-elohim` entry formerly listed this verse in error, and a correction is proposed in the wave-A central diff. The fire consumes the offering, wood, stones and dust and 'licked up' (*liḥēḵâ*) the water, which marks divine acceptance of the offering as in Lev 9:24 and 2 Chr 7:1 and settles the terms of v 24. Meteorological readings (lightning) are often proposed; the text names only the source.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('the fire of Yahweh fell') and reads it as a powerful beam directed from a craft hidden in the clouds. The line renders the Hebrew construct and verb literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּרְא֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: And all the people saw it, and they fell on their faces and said, "YHWH, he is the Elohim! YHWH, he is the Elohim!"

notes.official: *YHWH hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm, YHWH hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'YHWH, he is the Elohim!' The people's double confession answers v 24 and reverses the name of the prophet *ʾēliyyāhû* ('my El is Yah') (Cogan, *1 Kings*). Article per `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ לָהֶ֜ם תִּפְשׂ֣וּ ׀ אֶת־נְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל אִ֛ישׁ אַל־יִמָּלֵ֥ט מֵהֶ֖ם וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂ֑וּם וַיּוֹרִדֵ֤ם אֵלִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֔וֹן וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to them, "Seize the prophets of Ba'al; let not one of them escape." And they seized them, and Eliyahu brought them down to the brook Qishon and slaughtered them there.

notes.official: *wayyišḥāṭēm šām* 'and slaughtered them there': *šḥṭ* is the verb of slaughtering animals, sacrificial or not. The execution applies the Deuteronomic law on prophets of other gods (Deut 13:2-6; 17:2-7). Qishon = Kishon.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֙הוּ֙ לְאַחְאָ֔ב עֲלֵ֖ה אֱכֹ֣ל וּשְׁתֵ֑ה כִּי־ק֖וֹל הֲמ֥וֹן הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu said to Ach'av, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the rushing of rain."

notes.official: *qôl hămôn haggāšem*: *hāmôn* is 'roar, tumult, multitude' (BDB; HALOT). ASV 'the sound of abundance of rain' takes it as 'abundance'. The translation's 'the sound of the rushing of rain' takes it as the noise of a downpour (cf. NJPS 'the rumbling of rain'), the sense that fits *qôl* 'sound'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה אַחְאָ֖ב לֶאֱכֹ֣ל וְלִשְׁתּ֑וֹת וְאֵ֨לִיָּ֜הוּ עָלָ֨ה אֶל־רֹ֤אשׁ הַכַּרְמֶל֙ וַיִּגְהַ֣ר אַ֔רְצָה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם פָּנָ֖יו בֵּ֥ין ברכו [בִּרְכָּֽיו׃]

i18n.en: So Ach'av went up to eat and to drink. And Eliyahu went up to the top of Karmel, and he crouched down upon the earth and put his face between his knees.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *brkw* (defective) / Qere *birkāyw* 'his knees'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *wayyiḡhar* 'he crouched down' occurs elsewhere only in 2 Kgs 4:34-35 (Elisha over the boy); the posture is one of intercession.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל־נַעֲר֗וֹ עֲלֵֽה־נָא֙ הַבֵּ֣ט דֶּֽרֶךְ־יָ֔ם וַיַּ֙עַל֙ וַיַּבֵּ֔ט וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵ֣ין מְא֑וּמָה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שֻׁ֖ב שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he said to his servant, "Go up now, look toward the sea." And he went up and looked and said, "There is nothing." And he said, "Go again," seven times.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּשְּׁבִעִ֔ית וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה־עָ֛ב קְטַנָּ֥ה כְּכַף־אִ֖ישׁ עֹלָ֣ה מִיָּ֑ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֲלֵ֨ה אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־אַחְאָב֙ אֱסֹ֣ר וָרֵ֔ד וְלֹ֥א יַעַצָרְכָ֖ה הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass at the seventh time that he said, "Behold, a small cloud, like a man's palm, is rising from the sea." And he said, "Go up, say to Ach'av, 'Hitch up and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.'"

notes.official: *ʿāḇ qəṭannâ kəḵap̄-ʾîš ʿōlâ mîyyām* 'a small cloud, like a man's palm, rising from the sea': rain in the Levant comes from the west, off the Mediterranean, the view from Karmel's ridge.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ עַד־כֹּ֣ה וְעַד־כֹּ֗ה וְהַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ הִֽתְקַדְּרוּ֙ עָבִ֣ים וְר֔וּחַ וַיְהִ֖י גֶּ֣שֶׁם גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּרְכַּ֥ב אַחְאָ֖ב וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ יִזְרְעֶֽאלָה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass in a little while that the skies grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ach'av rode and went to Yizre'el.

notes.official: *wəhaššāmayim hiṯqaddərû ʿāḇîm wərûaḥ* 'the skies grew black with clouds and wind': *šāmayim* per the central `shamayim` ('skies'); *rûaḥ* here is physical wind. Yizre'el = Jezreel, Ach'av's second residence.

paragraphs.text: וְיַד־יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ וַיְשַׁנֵּ֖ס מָתְנָ֑יו וַיָּ֙רָץ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אַחְאָ֔ב עַד־בֹּאֲכָ֖ה יִזְרְעֶֽאלָה׃

i18n.en: And the hand of YHWH was on Eliyahu; and he girded up his loins and ran before Ach'av to the entrance of Yizre'el.

notes.official: *wəyaḏ-YHWH hāyəṯâ ʾel-ʾēliyyāhû* 'And the hand of YHWH was on Eliyahu' (`yad-yhwh`): the idiom for prophetic empowerment (2 Kgs 3:15; Ezek 1:3). Running before the king's chariot is the role of a royal outrunner (1 Sam 8:11; 2 Sam 15:1).
